Fats in games Ok, I did my degree in this shit. Let me educate you, fatties! You don't get fat characters in games because they aren't appealing to look at. They wouldn't be able to run realistically with a gunt in the way of their knees. You could apply some crazy physics to the gunt wasting a LOT of time and processing power, or you could just have a human sized character. Why bother wasting time, effort and money making realistic gunt/fat roll physics for a games engine when it would only put all your potential players off your game.

Try animating a fat person climbing a mountain face with a huge gunt in the way, it's unnecessarily difficult and will never look good, even if it looks convincing. Imagine having to even make a fat model for a character, who'd want to look at reference images of a fat fuck anyway. No one would get excited about that. It'd be too difficult to make a character gain weight without it looking like the mesh is corrupting, Fable 3 and The Sims had to limit how fat characters could get because theres only so much vertices can deform without graphical problems.

Besides, morbidly obese people don't have a structured form like human sized people do. Some get lots of back fat, others it's mostly in the gunt, knees end up being innies etc. A fat character on the box art would put people off, fat is repulsive and unnecessary. End of story.
